article.title: A recipient received the same message twice
article.excerpt: Almost always this is a client-side timeout followed by a resend. Here is how to confirm it, and how to stop it happening.

p: Two sends with the same recipient and nearly identical timestamps, both accepted, is the signature of a retry. There is no idempotency key, so the platform has no way to treat the second request as the same message — it is a new message, sent and billed.

steps.p: Set the time window around the incident and add the number.
Seconds apart means a resend. Far apart means two separate requests from your side.
Two distinct platform IDs with two provider IDs confirms two independent sends.

list: Treat a client-side timeout as unknown, not as failure — the message may already be on its way.
If a request times out, look it up in the log by time window and recipient instead of resending.
De-duplicate on your side before calling the API: record that you intended to send, then reconcile against the log.
sections.note: Duplicate prevention has to live in the caller. The platform deliberately offers no idempotency key, so a retry is never silently swallowed.
